newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers on corporate dollar selling.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers on corporate dollar selling.

text.p: The ringgit recovered from its lows against the dollar on local corporate selling of the dollar, dealers said on Thursday.
"Dollar/ringgit was capped at 2.6400. There were a lot of dollar selling orders from local corporates at that level," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Buying of the ringgit/Singapore dollar cross had also capped dollar/ringgit, he said.
Dealers said profit-taking and some selling out of London helped push dollar/ringgit to its intra-day low of 2.6260 before renewed offshore buying surfaced.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6315/45 to a dollar.
The ringgit was earlier pressured by month-end commercial demand for the dollar and sales by U.S. funds on continuing worries about Thailand's economic troubles.
Dealers said currencies in the region were being driven by the baht and sentiment was likely to remain jumpy ahead of the Thai government's rescue package for the ailing economy, due by August 5.
They said until Thailand settled down, the turmoil in regional currencies was expected to continue.
